correctness.rationale: For fixed 2-support H, a zero is permissible exactly at cells with row-H degree plus column-H degree equal to one. All other nondefender cells are forced ones. The proof rigorously classifies every potentially isolated positive vertex: a lone defender or the uniquely uncovered row-column corner of a near-spanning bipartite matching. Summing optional ones produces every coefficient exactly once. A row-count lower bound with equality classification proves the minimum, including the exceptional 2-by-2 case. Independent literal-definition brute-force tested all 617544 ternary configurations on six boards and agreed coefficientwise; 4x4 and 4x5 support enumerations agree with optimum predictions. Finite tests do not prove the theorem.
